page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the c4 family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 372 GB of system memory, translating to 7.75 GB of RAM per core. It contains no local storage and does not include any GPU accelerators. The CPU features an L3 cache of 260 MB, alongside advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512).

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-highmem-48 demonstrates strong performance across multiple domains. It achieves top-tier results in text processing and image processing, alongside high throughput in single-threaded text generation for small language models. General CPU capabilities are strong, as evidenced by its PassMark CPU score of 57,593.71 and high multi-threaded decompression speeds. Memory bandwidth is measured at 144.15 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 61.96 GB/sec for large block write operations. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware results in a performance tradeoff for larger AI workloads; while prompt processing for a 70B model remains average, text generation for the same model falls into the weak category at 2.74 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions provides a qualitative advantage for CPU-based deep learning tasks without the added cost of a dedicated GPU.
